title: What does a $22 hour really pay?
hook: The app says $22 an hour. Is that what the hour is worth to you?

knows: that driving a car costs money
doesNotKnow: that the costs of earning shrink what an hour pays
how to turn a per-mile cost into a per-hour cost

misconception: $22 an hour is what a driving job pays me.
objective: The learner can subtract per-hour costs (miles × cost per mile) from hourly pay and explain why pay after the costs of earning it is the number to compare.

claims.text: At $22 an hour, 15 miles an hour and $0.50 a mile, driving costs $7.50 an hour and $14.50 is left.
At 15 miles an hour, $0.25 a mile leaves $18.25 and $0.70 a mile leaves $11.50.
A car's fuel and wear are costs that grow with every mile driven.
claims.source: Per-mile operating costs (fuel, maintenance, tyres, mileage-driven depreciation): AAA, 'Your Driving Costs' (annual). The lesson's $0.25 / $0.50 / $0.70 are illustrative, not AAA's or an official rate.

claims.text: The lesson is a model that ignores tax and tips; the per-mile costs are examples, not an official rate.
claims.source: Stage chip 'Model: no tax, no tips'; reveal's last line.

recall.question: A job pays $30 an hour. You drive 20 miles each hour, at $0.60 a mile in car costs. What does an hour leave you, before tax?
recall.why: 20 × $0.60 = $12 of driving costs each hour, so $30 − $12 = $18 is left. Earnings are what remains after the costs of earning them.
